history.answer: My vision has been getting cloudy and blurry over the past few years, doctor. It feels like I am looking through a dirty or fogged-up window all the time.
It started about three years ago and has been very gradually getting worse over time. It did not happen suddenly.
It affects both of my eyes, but when I cover one eye at a time, my right eye is noticeably blurrier than my left.
No, it has never gone completely black or cleared up temporarily. The fogginess is constant throughout the day.
Everything just looks hazy and washed out all over. I do not have a dark blind spot in the middle, my side vision is fine, and straight lines still look straight.
Distance vision is much more blurry, but strangely, I can read books up close without my reading glasses lately. Getting a new pair of distance glasses two years ago barely helped.
Yes, oncoming headlights glare terribly when I drive at night, and I see large glowing halos around streetlamps. It makes driving in the dark very uncomfortable.
Yes, colors seem faded and somewhat yellowish or brownish, like looking through an aged filter. They do not look vibrant anymore.
No, I have not noticed any floating specks, flashes of light, or dark curtains coming over my sight.
No, I do not see double images. Things are just blurry and lack sharpness.
No, my eyelids are not drooping, my vision does not get worse toward the evening, and I have no trouble chewing or swallowing.
No, my eyes do not hurt at all, they do not ache when I move them, and there is no redness.
No, I have not had any new headaches, no tenderness over my temples, and no jaw ache when chewing.
No, I have had no weakness or numbness in my arms or legs, no slurred speech, and no dizziness.
No, I have never had an injury to my eyes or head.
I have had high blood pressure for about ten years, which has stayed well controlled with my daily pill. I do not have diabetes, and my last eye exam was several years ago.
I have mild high cholesterol, but I do not have irregular heartbeats, atrial fibrillation, or any known blockage in my neck arteries.
No, I never had severe nearsightedness, I was never diagnosed with glaucoma, and I have never had any eye surgery.
No, I have never taken steroid medications, malaria pills, or tuberculosis drugs.
My mother had cataracts in her late seventies, but no one in my family has had glaucoma or macular degeneration.
I had to stop driving at night completely because of the blinding glare, and watching television or reading street signs is getting harder, though luckily I have not fallen.
I thought maybe my eyes were just getting clouded over with dirt or that my glasses lenses were worn out and scratched.
I'm really worried the DMV will take away my driver's license because the blinding glare from headlights makes driving at night terrifying.
I was hoping to see if a simple lens procedure can clear away the fog so I can keep driving to see my grandkids.
Aside from high blood pressure and mild high cholesterol, I have no other chronic medical conditions.
I have never had any operations and I have never been admitted to the hospital.
I take lisinopril 10 milligrams once every morning for my blood pressure. I do not take any over-the-counter supplements or eye drops.
No, I have no known allergies to any medications, foods, or materials.
No, I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco products.
I only drink a glass of wine on special occasions, maybe once a month at most.
I am a retired accountant living at home with my wife, and I keep an active lifestyle with daily neighborhood walks.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 128/78 mmHg, heart rate 70 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, body temperature 36.6 °C, and oxygen saturation 98% on ambient air.
Well-nourished elderly male in no acute distress, alert and ambulatory without assistance.
Sclerae are white and non-icteric; conjunctivae are pink and clear bilaterally without injection or discharge.

Distant visual acuity 20/70 right eye and 20/50 left eye with slight pinhole improvement; ophthalmoscopy reveals dull red reflex and prominent brownish-yellow nuclear lens opacities worse on the right; pupils are equally round and reactive to light without afferent pupillary defect; confrontation visual fields are full; Amsler grid shows no central distortion; fundus visualization is mildly hazy but optic discs and maculae appear anatomically normal.
Extraocular movements are full and smooth in all directions without pain, diplopia, or eyelid ptosis.
Bilateral superficial temporal arteries are non-tender, soft, compressible, and normally pulsatile without scalp tenderness.
